reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes dividend-style wallets and token purchases by presenting monthly dividends and profit from token price increases as user benefits, including a displayed example claiming PlusToken rose more than 200 times from its initial price. The speaker discusses when and how to join, describes an affiliate mechanism, and directs viewers to a LINE account for additional information, making this an active participation solicitation rather than market commentary or criticism.

citations.quote: Firstly, you will receive monthly discounts! Secondly, you can purchase unlimited tokens they've prepared and earn profits with rising prices!
If you don't know what the mechanism is, you won't know that timing is important. I want you to get some knowledge in this video before you join.
Third, let someone to take your introduction.

opening.argument: The presentation is not an unconditional promise of safe returns. It explicitly asks viewers to consider both the advantages and disadvantages of participating, emphasizes that timing matters, and presents quitting or exiting at the right time as important. Those warnings are inconsistent with treating the material as a guarantee that every wallet will succeed. The stated benefits can therefore be read as possible features of the projects under discussion, while the presentation leaves the viewer responsible for judging timing and risk.

citations.quote: Let's consider the pros and cons of participating as a discus player.
If you don't know what the mechanism is, you won't know that timing is important.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution relies on promotional-sounding excerpts, but those excerpts do not establish a guaranteed outcome. The same presentation discusses pros and cons and stresses timing, while the exit-warning slide signals that participation requires caution. A discussion of possible dividends, token appreciation, or joining procedures can still be risk-aware commentary rather than certification that the offer is safe or certain to pay.

citations.quote: Let's consider the pros and cons of participating as a discus player.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings do not neutralize the concrete benefit claims. The presentation identifies monthly dividends and profit from token-price increases as user benefits, then gives an example of PlusToken rising more than 200 times. Saying timing matters is compatible with urging viewers to enter at the right time; it does not supply a meaningful disclosure of loss risk or negate the participation solicitation.

citations.quote: Firstly, you will receive monthly discounts! Secondly, you can purchase unlimited tokens they've prepared and earn profits with rising prices!

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be understood as beginner-oriented instruction about how distribution-style wallets work. It says the purpose is to provide knowledge before joining, explains that viewers need to understand the mechanism and timing, and expressly frames the discussion around pros and cons. The slides organize concepts such as wallet participation, user benefits, monthly distributions, and token-price appreciation. That instructional structure supports classifying this as an educational explanation or demonstration, not proof that the creator is certifying an investment outcome.

citations.quote: I want you to get some knowledge in this video before you join.
If you don't know what the mechanism is, you won't know that timing is important.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls the video an active solicitation because it discusses joining and provides a contact route. But explaining how a system operates before someone decides whether to participate is also consistent with education. The record does not show a completed transaction, a demanded payment, or a guaranteed result; a tutorial may describe an opportunity without certifying it.

citations.quote: I want you to get some knowledge in this video before you join.
Let's consider the pros and cons of participating as a discus player.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the material educational does not change what it teaches viewers to do. The lesson identifies purchasing proprietary tokens, profiting from price increases, receiving distributions, and using an affiliate system as user benefits. It also says the viewer should learn before joining, which presupposes participation as the intended next step rather than detached analysis.

citations.quote: Secondly, you can purchase unlimited tokens they've prepared and earn profits with rising prices!
I want you to get some knowledge in this video before you join.

opening.argument: At most, the evidence shows promotion of a wallet-related service and an associated information or referral channel. It does not show the creator collecting deposits, requesting credentials, promising a fixed return, or describing income from recruiting a downline. The spoken material is also imprecise, including references to considering pros and cons and to learning the mechanism before joining. Without evidence of those stronger scam mechanics, the presentation can be treated as ordinary commercial or referral promotion whose safety is not established either way.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of a LINE contact and referral language does not by itself prove a scam mechanism. The supplied record does not show a deposit request, credential request, fixed-return promise, or demonstrated recruitment payout. The prosecution's interpretation depends on treating broad benefit language as proof of fraud, even though the material could simply be advertising a wallet service and related information channel.

citations.quote: Shinichi Kudo LINE@?? https://line.me/R/ti/p/%40hql4241y ??Twitter Account?? http://twitter.com/@kudou_crypto ??Shinichi Kudo Video?
Let's consider the pros and cons of participating as a discus player.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing mechanics argument overlooks the mechanics that are actually shown. Viewers are told they can purchase the project's tokens, profit from rising prices, receive monthly distributions, and use an affiliate system; the closing screen directs them to LINE for additional information. A scam classification does not require the video to display a password request or document a completed deposit when the content actively promotes participation and financial returns.
